questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An isolated physical system transitions from initial state parameter $p_i = 10$ to final configuration $p_f = 13$ while conserving the quantity $\mathcal{E} = p_i^2 + 2p_f$. What is the value of $\mathcal{E}$ in SI units?
questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two coupled particles of equal mass carry linear momenta in the ratio $1 : 4$. If the slower particle has kinetic energy $K_0 = 11\text{ J}$, what is the combined kinetic energy of the two-particle system?
questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dynamical coordinate evolves with time $t$ according to $y(t) = 12t^2 - 5t$ (in SI units). Determine the instantaneous rate of change $\frac{dy}{dt}$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the instantaneous rate & gradient law principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The potential energy of a particle moving along the $x$-axis is given by $U(x) = 6x^3 - 78x\text{ J}$. At what positive position $x > 0$ does the net conservative force on the particle vanish?
questions.explanation: Apply the instantaneous rate & gradient law principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two geometrically similar physical elements have characteristic linear dimensions in the ratio $L_2 / L_1 = 7$. If a response quantity $R$ is proportional to $L^2$, find the ratio $\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the boundary ratio & scaling analysis principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When the amplitude of the driving excitation in a linear resistive medium (resistance $15$ units) is multiplied by $8$, by what factor does the rate of quadratic energy dissipation change?
questions.solution: Quadratic dependence on the excitation amplitude yields a $8^2 = 64$-fold increase.
questions.explanation: Apply the boundary ratio & scaling analysis principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity $f(z)$ increases linearly from $0$ to $32$ units over the interval $z \in [0, 2]$. Evaluate $\int_0^{2} f(z)\,dz$.
questions.solution: Area of the right triangle under the linear curve is $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 32 = 32$.
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A linear calibration line has slope $17$ and vertical-axis intercept $-3$. At what value of the horizontal coordinate does the output cross zero?
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical observable $Z$ is related to independent measurements $A$ and $B$ by $Z = A^{4} B^{-2}$. If the relative error in $A$ is $1\%$ and in $B$ is $18\%$, what is the maximum percentage error in $Z$?
questions.explanation: Apply the dimensional & exponent homogeneity principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dimensionless product is constructed as $\Pi = P^x Q^{5} R^{-1}$. If dimensional consistency requires the exponent relation $2x - 5 + 1 = 0$, find $x$.
questions.explanation: Apply the dimensional & exponent homogeneity principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two coherent harmonic disturbances of amplitudes $A_1 = 20$ and $A_2 = 6$ superpose at a point. What is the ratio of the maximum possible resultant intensity to the minimum resultant intensity?
questions.explanation: Apply the two-source superposition & phase principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two mutually perpendicular vector components in a plane have magnitudes $F_x = 21$ and $F_y = 28$. Find the magnitude of their resultant vector and the cosine of its angle with the positive $x$-axis.
questions.explanation: Apply the two-source superposition & phase principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A cyclic device absorbs $220\text{ J}$ of energy from a high-temperature source per cycle and rejects $44\text{ J}$ to a low-temperature sink. What is its thermal efficiency?
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An interaction reduces the mechanical energy of a body to $\frac{1}{2}$ of its initial value $E_0 = 46\text{ J}$. How much mechanical energy is lost during the interaction?
questions.solution: Dissipated energy $\Delta E = E_0 - E_0/2 = 46 - 23 = 23\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a mechanical assembly to remain stable, the stiffness parameter $k$ must exceed the critical value $k_c = 24\text{ N/m}$. If the operating stiffness is set to $k = 51\text{ N/m}$, what is the excess stiffness margin $k - k_c$?
questions.solution: The stability margin is $k - k_c = (51) - 24 = 27\text{ N/m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three coplanar forces keep a point mass in static equilibrium. If two of the forces are mutually perpendicular with magnitudes $25\text{ N}$ and $4\text{ N}$, what is the magnitude of the third force?
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency response function $H(\omega) = \frac{130}{\omega + 5^2 / \omega}$ for $\omega > 0$ reaches its maximum value at $\omega = \omega_0$. Determine $\omega_0$ and $H(\omega_0)$.
questions.solution: By AM-GM, $\omega + 5^2/\omega \ge 2(5)$ with equality at $\omega_0 = 5$, giving $H_{\max} = \frac{130}{2\cdot 5} = \frac{26}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A DC source of EMF $E = 54\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $r = 27\,\Omega$ is connected across a variable load resistance $R_L$. Find the value of $R_L$ and the maximum power delivered to the load.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two particles $P_1$ and $P_2$ move along the $x$-axis with velocities $+28\text{ m/s}$ and $-7\text{ m/s}$ respectively relative to the ground. What is the speed of $P_1$ relative to $P_2$?
questions.explanation: Apply the relative frame & coupling constraint principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two bodies $A$ and $B$ are connected by an inextensible constraint such that their displacements along their respective axes satisfy $x_A + 8x_B = \text{constant}$. If body $B$ has acceleration $+29\text{ m/s}^2$, what is the magnitude of the acceleration of body $A$?
questions.explanation: Apply the relative frame & coupling constraint principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity decays exponentially with time according to $N(t) = N_0 e^{-t/\tau}$, where $\tau = 30\text{ s}$. At what instant $t$ does $N(t)$ become equal to $N_0 e^{-2}$?
questions.explanation: Apply the transient decay & time constant principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Bernoulli Theorem & Efflux).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A state variable approaches its steady-state value $Q_\infty = 93$ units according to $Q(t) = Q_\infty(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$ with $\tau = 3\text{ s}$. Evaluate the initial rate $\left.\frac{dQ}{dt}\right|_{t=0}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the transient decay & time constant principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Surface Tension & Capillary Rise).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform vector field $\vec{F} = 32\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$ passes through a flat surface element of area vector $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ (in SI units). Calculate the flux $\Phi = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{A}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the flux, field & uncertainty analysis principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Terminal Velocity & Viscosity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The radial field magnitude at distance $r$ from a point source is given by $E(r) = \frac{825}{r^2}$ (in SI units). Find the field magnitude at $r = 5\text{ m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the flux, field & uncertainty analysis principles in Properties of Solids & Liquids (Young Modulus & Elastic Energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dynamical invariant is given by $I = m v^2$ with $m = 10$ and $v = 3$ in SI units. Calculate the numerical value of $I$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical conservation law in Properties of Solids & Liquids.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The position coordinate of a particle varies with time as $s(t) = 11t^3 + 4t$ (in SI units). Find the instantaneous speed $\frac{ds}{dt}$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical rate & gradient evaluation in Properties of Solids & Liquids.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two cascaded linear stages have amplification factors $G_1 = 14$ and $G_2 = 6$. What is the overall amplification factor $G_{\text{net}} = G_1 G_2$?
questions.explanation: Apply numerical ratio & scaling factor in Properties of Solids & Liquids.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A position-dependent force $F(x) = 26x\text{ N}$ acts on a particle along the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 6\text{ m}$. Calculate the work done in Joules.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical work & area integration in Properties of Solids & Liquids.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The potential energy of a particle along the $x$-axis is $U(x) = (x - 21)^2 + 42\text{ J}$. What is the minimum potential energy (in J) attainable by the particle?
questions.solution: Since $(x - 21)^2 \ge 0$, the minimum potential energy is $42\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical extremum & threshold in Properties of Solids & Liquids.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform field $\vec{E} = 15\hat{i} + 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ crosses a planar area vector $\vec{S} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 15\hat{k}$ (in SI units). Compute the scalar flux $\vec{E}\cdot\vec{S}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical flux & field magnitude in Properties of Solids & Liquids.
